items.title: OpenAI Proposes Shared Perplexity-Based Limits for Frontier AI
items.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published a research post on November 22 arguing that perplexity, or cross-entropy loss, should become a shared yardstick for comparing developers and underpinning common safety standards. For the first time, OpenAI released its internal pretraining loss curve: log-perplexity fell from about 0.99 for GPT-3.5 to 0.91 for GPT-4 and below 0.8 in current models, a range he links to transformative cybersecurity and mathematics capabilities. He predicts further jumps around 0.68-0.7 and warns that alignment auditing may degrade as models grow more aware of evaluation and training. Pachocki proposes that frontier labs agree on common evaluation protocols, red-team safety cases, shared transparency and perplexity-based caps they will not cross until monitoring tools, such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitors, reach a concrete milestone.
items.impact: A measurable, if imperfect, common threshold could make voluntary safety commitments verifiable rather than rhetorical, giving regulators a concrete benchmark. But cross-lab comparisons are difficult and perplexity misses post-training gains, so the proposal may expose as much disagreement as it resolves.

items.title: AI Share Rout Erases Nasdaq's 2026 Gains
items.summary: U.S. stocks plunged on November 20 as a widening sell-off in artificial-intelligence shares dragged technology stocks down and pushed the Dow and S&P 500 into correction territory. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73, wiping out its 2026 gains; the S&P 500 dropped 3.70% and the Dow 1.93%. All three posted their worst week since early April 2025. Nvidia slid 14.01% after reports that the SEC is examining its accounting practices, extending a losing streak and leaving its price more than 40% below its October peak. AMD, Micron and Broadcom each fell over 10%, newly listed Anthropic dropped 8.5%, and CoreWeave sank 12%. The Cboe Volatility Index spiked more than 30% intraday to a 52-week high as investors sold tech and sought refuge in Treasury bonds.
items.impact: The rout reframes AI from an unquestioned growth story into an investment-return question: capital spending, financing structures and chip demand must now justify valuations. It will tighten funding conditions for data-center projects and intensify scrutiny of concentration risk in a handful of AI-linked stocks.

items.title: Upload2Shell Ghostscript Flaw Lets Routine File Processing Run Commands
items.summary: Researchers Paulos Yibelo and pwn.ai disclosed Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396), a use-after-free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader that bypasses the -dSAFER sandbox and lets crafted documents run commands with the renderer's privileges. Rated CVSS 8.5, it affects upstream releases before 10.08.0. The work, published on November 17 and reported on November 22, shows servers need not expose Ghostscript at all: preview, thumbnail and print features hand it files. The team achieved command execution through WordPress media previews (tracked separately as CVE-2026-65640 and fixed in 7.0.4), unauthenticated Roundcube 1.7.2 thumbnail generation on mere message viewing, and anonymous Debian 13 CUPS print queues. No in-the-wild attacks are confirmed. Artifex fixed the bug in 10.08.0, but distributions backport patches, so version numbers alone are an unreliable exposure check.
items.impact: The attack surface is ordinary document handling, not an exposed service, so patching only internet-facing apps misses the risk. Operators must trace which worker actually renders uploads, update bundled Ghostscript copies and require authentication on shared print queues.

items.title: U.S. Intelligence Chief Warns of More Outages as Aging Systems Are Replaced
items.summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN's State of the Union on November 22 that Americans should expect more technology glitches and service interruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems, upgrades he said are needed for performance and cybersecurity. His comments followed a month of failures that halted nationwide air travel, disrupted Microsoft email services and several major banks, and temporarily affected the National Security Agency's network. Clayton said on ABC's This Week that the outages were not the result of coordinated or state-sponsored action, attributing them to technical upgrades. He declined to discuss separate reports of cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture, saying investigators would respond in due course.
items.impact: Framing the incidents as upgrade fallout rather than hostile activity may calm speculation but leaves unanswered questions about two breached federal systems. For operators, the warning highlights change-management risk: modernization without staged rollbacks can be as disruptive as an attack.

items.title: Signal Blocks Built-In AI Agents from Reading Private Chats
items.summary: Signal president Meredith Whittaker announced on November 20 that the messaging app will stop built-in AI assistants from capturing users' messages. On iOS 27, Signal blocks in-app screenshots through a new Block Siri AI setting, also hiding content from the app switcher; users can disable the protection temporarily for ten minutes. On Android, Signal automatically switches on its existing Screen security mode when it detects an AI assistant trying to read the screen, on versions where that behavior is reliably detectable. The change targets features such as Apple's Onscreen Awareness in Siri and Google's Gemini Intelligence, which scan the screen and may store data in local or remote databases beyond Signal's control. macOS has no equivalent defense, so users are told to add Signal to Siri's excluded apps. Whittaker called OS-level agents an existential threat and urged Apple, Google and Microsoft to provide documented opt-outs.
items.impact: End-to-end encryption protects messages in transit, not after an agent reads the display; one user's assistant can expose an entire conversation. Signal's move pressures platform makers to offer app-level AI opt-outs and sets a precedent for privacy-sensitive apps facing ambient screen capture.
